abstract_sentences.text: Ultra-long generation by large language models (LLMs) is a widely demanded scenario, yet it remains a significant challenge due to their maximum generation length limit and overall quality degradation as sequence length increases.

evidence.anchor: maximum generation length limit and overall quality degradation

abstract_sentences.text: Previous approaches, exemplified by LongWriter (Bai et al., 2025), typically involve supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on synthetic long-form outputs.

evidence.anchor: Previous approaches ... involve supervised fine-tuning

abstract_sentences.text: However, this strategy heavily depends on synthetic SFT data, which is difficult and costly to construct, often lacks coherence and consistency, and tends to be overly artificial and structurally monotonous.

evidence.anchor: difficult and costly to construct ... structurally monotonous

abstract_sentences.text: In this work, we propose an incentivization-based approach that, starting entirely from scratch and without relying on any annotated or synthetic data, leverages reinforcement learning (RL) to foster the emergence of ultra-long, high-quality text generation capabilities in LLMs.

evidence.anchor: starting entirely from scratch and without relying on any annotated or synthetic data

abstract_sentences.text: We perform RL training starting from a base model, similar to R1-Zero, guiding it to engage in reasoning that facilitates planning and refinement during the writing process.

evidence.anchor: reasoning that facilitates planning and refinement

abstract_sentences.text: To support this, we employ specialized reward models that steer the LLM towards improved length control, writing quality, and structural formatting.

evidence.anchor: improved length control, writing quality, and structural formatting

abstract_sentences.text: Experimental evaluations show that our LongWriter-Zero model, trained from Qwen2.5-32B, consistently outperforms traditional SFT methods on long-form writing tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results across all metrics on WritingBench and Arena-Write, and even surpassing 100B+ models such as DeepSeek R1 and Qwen3-235B.

evidence.anchor: state-of-the-art results across all metrics ... surpassing 100B+ models
Ultra-long text generation that extends over thousands of words
it comes with two critical limitations
using reinforcement learning to activate long-form generation abilities in LLMs from scratch
three key research questions
all three components—reward design, test-time scaling, and continual pretraining—are critical

equation_theory_inventory.label: Eq. (1)
equation_theory_inventory.statement: Group-relative advantage A_i equals reward minus group mean divided by group standard deviation.

evidence.anchor: advantage for the ith sample scored with ri

equation_theory_inventory.label: Eq. (2)
equation_theory_inventory.statement: GRPO maximizes the group average of clipped importance-ratio terms minus beta times KL divergence to a fixed reference policy; ratio is pi_theta(o_i|q)/pi_theta_old(o_i|q).

evidence.anchor: GRPO then maximizes the clipped objective

equation_theory_inventory.label: Eq. (3)
equation_theory_inventory.statement: Piecewise Length RM reward is 1 in [L_lower,L_upper], linear relative reward below L_lower, and linear over-length penalty using L_max above L_upper.

evidence.anchor: outputs falling within this length range ... receive higher rewards

equation_theory_inventory.label: Eq. (4)
equation_theory_inventory.statement: Bradley-Terry preference loss maximizes the sigmoid margin between reward for human-preferred y_w and rejected y_l.

evidence.anchor: following the Bradley–Terry model to model preferences

equation_theory_inventory.label: Eq. (5)
equation_theory_inventory.statement: Final advantage is the average of normalized length, writing, and format advantages.

evidence.anchor: advantage-level averaging

claim_closure.claim: RL can activate ultra-long writing from a base model without synthetic/annotated SFT output data.
claim_closure.method_response: GRPO from Qwen2.5-32B with Length/Writing/Format reward signals and no supervised long-output SFT stage.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 2–4, Table 1, and A.8 show RL/SFT comparisons; however Writing RM uses manually labeled preferences and CP includes 1% distilled Base-think CoT.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion calls this the first RL-only attempt, but does not reconcile the broad no-annotated/no-synthetic wording.

evidence.anchor: without relying on any annotated or synthetic data
trained on manually-labeled preference data

claim_closure.claim: RQ1 composite reward design guides long-form generation.
claim_closure.method_response: Length RM, Writing RM, Format RM, normalization and Eq. (5) provide a computable composite signal.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Base-nothink curves improve; no per-RM deletion, reward calibration, or independent human-validity test.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion states tailored reward design is essential.

evidence.anchor: normalization-then-aggregation scheme
demonstrate the effectiveness of our reward design

claim_closure.claim: RQ2 long CoT improves RL-based long-form writing.
claim_closure.method_response: Think Prompt requires planning/refinement inside `<think>` before `<answer>` and is compared with Direct-Answer.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 2/3, Table 1 w/o Thinking, and Figure 6 all favor Think, but no seed or compute-matched prompt-only control isolates the mechanism.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion recovers explicit reasoning as improving planning and coherence.

evidence.anchor: comprehensive and in-depth planning

claim_closure.claim: RQ3 continual pretraining raises the RL performance ceiling.
claim_closure.method_response: 30B-token long-form corpus plus 1% Base-think long CoT precedes the same GRPO.
claim_closure.evidence_response: CP-think starts above 1,000 and reaches around 1,400 Elo; the w/o CP row is lower, but CP changes both writing priors and distilled format alignment.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion states continual pretraining substantially raises RL ceilings.

final_judgment.single_storyline: LongWriter-Zero treats ultra-long writing as an open-ended policy-optimization problem: group-relative RL with length, writing and format rewards, then Think Prompt and continual pretraining to improve learnability and the base-model ceiling.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: Keep the RQs, GRPO Eq. (1)–(2), Length RM Eq. (3), Writing RM Eq. (4), final reward Eq. (5), three setup curves, Table 1, Figures 2–6, SFT/RL comparison and automatic/human win-rate summaries; these answer why, how and headline performance.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A.2–A.5 moves filtering, length prompt, CP data and judge rubric; A.6–A.10 moves reward-hacking failures, extra scale/baselines, LongBench and nine pages of cases. This preserves the conceptual line but weakens statistical and reproducibility self-sufficiency.
final_judgment.best_pattern: The strongest pattern is a compact formula-to-plot chain: Eq. (1)–(2) define GRPO, Eq. (3)–(5) define the composite reward, Figures 2–4 track the same step axis and component comparisons, Table 1 concentrates domain/requirement/Elo decisions, and A.10 makes Think versus Answer concrete.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The largest gap is between broad RL-only/SOTA language and the evidence boundary: manual preference data and distilled CoT contradict the literal no-annotated/no-synthetic claim, CP mixes two mechanisms, uncertainty is unnamed, and factuality/long-range consistency are not directly tested.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For open-ended RL writing, define every reward source and unit in the main text, then separate reward efficacy from reward validity with component, seed-level and compute-matched tests plus per-task distributions.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule applies when outputs, reward components and task distributions are observable. Private preference data, external judges and evolving user goals still require provenance, contamination checks, judge-validity analysis and human auditing; Elo or critic aggregates cannot stand in for factuality or deployment safety.
